messages:
Maria S: Heads-up: planning KEK rotation across AWS/GCP/Azure next week. Thinking about using alias shadowing and per-envelope header versioning. Thoughts?
Kevin L: +1 to alias shadowing and header versioning. Plan: create alias `alias/redwood-kek-v2`, keep `alias/redwood-kek` pointing at old key until cutover, and dual-read during canary.
Sanjay P: We should run a rewrap canary first — pick ~100 users embeddings, re-encrypt with v2 and run parity checks. Watch Redis/embedding caches and any KV caches that store ciphertext.
Elaine C: RBAC note: we'll need to update service accounts/roles so processes can access both keys during the window. Terraform changes to add `kms:Encrypt`/`kms:Decrypt` + GCP `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt` equivalents. How do we validate the permission change safely?
Kevin L: For validation: run a permission smoke that calls `Encrypt`/`Decrypt`/`GenerateDataKey` against each provider and assert success. Also export audit logs for those ops to the SIEM. Audit index fields: principal, key_alias, op, src_ip, timestamp. Retention: 1 year for now.
Maria S: Important: our envelope format includes an object header with `kek_alias` and `hdr_v`. We'll bump `hdr_v` to `2` for v2-encrypted objects. Rewrap job must update header atomically to avoid mixups.
Sanjay P: Prefer write-new-and-swap (create new ciphertext + new header, then atomically update pointer). That makes rollback easier — we can point back to old object if something fails.
Elaine C: Deployment plan sketch: canary rewrap -> staggered per-shard -> roll forward if parity checks pass. Sample decrypt test for AWS: ```bash
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --output text | base64 --decode
```
security-bot: Checklist: 1) RBAC reviewed by security 2) Audit export to SIEM enabled for Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey 3) Ensure backups and snapshots remain decryptable (both keys) 4) Run vuln-scan on rewrap job image 5) Add monitoring for failed decrypt rates.
infra-bot: CI job created: `infra/rewrap-canary` pipeline -> triggers on tag `rewrap/v2`. Link: https://ci.internal/pipe/123 (runs rewrap for sample shard and report parity).
Kevin L: Also add dual-decode fallback in the service for a transition window: try hdr_v==2 decode first, if fails, attempt decode with v1 keys for N days. Log both attempts to audit.
Maria S: Cloud vendor quirks: Azure Key Vault has `wrapKey`/`unwrapKey` semantics and soft-delete/purge protection. Make sure we don't purge old key material until all rewraps+TTL expire.\nSanjay P: Embedding cache TTLs matter. Option A: invalidate caches on rewrap (expensive). Option B: implement dual-decode for TTL window (less disruptive). I vote dual-decode + cache invalidation on mismatch.
Elaine C: Emergency rotate play (if compromise suspected): create v3 alias, stop issuing new encrypts with old v1, prioritize high-rate rewrap job with throttling, page oncall, rotate service principal keys as well. Document rollback criteria.
Maria S: Add an automated smoke check: pick a small sample, run decrypt tests across AWS/GCP/Azure, verify audit entries for each decrypt/rewrap. Fail the rollout if parity mismatches > 0.5%.
Kevin L: I'll draft the runbook and include a small script to validate audit log entries and sample decrypts. Will post in docs/rewrap-runbooks.
Elaine C: I'll open a Terraform PR for the RBAC delta and schedule the canary for next Tue 10:00 PST.
Maria S: Thanks all — action items: Elaine PR for RBAC, Kevin runbook + scripts, infra to monitor CI job and parity alerts. Ping @security-bot when PR ready for review.
